description: One social or messaging identity for a person or organization -- typically an entry in a contact.card socialHandles array. platform alone identifies nobody, so at least one of handle, platformId, or url is also required.

$kind.description: Optional self-identifier (cf. GraphQL __typename). Omit when the enclosing schema already names the role -- an entry inside a socialHandles array is unambiguously a social handle by virtue of the array it lives in. Include only when this object might appear untyped outside its normal context.

contexts.description: Free-text roles this handle serves, e.g. ["personal"], ["work"], ["support"] (JSContact-style) -- WHERE this handle is used.

handle.description: Display handle WITHOUT the leading "@" -- store "jdoe", not "@jdoe"; the "@" is presentation, added by consumers that render it. Federated platforms (Mastodon, Bluesky, etc.) need the full user@instance.tld form -- a bare name is ambiguous across instances.

metadata.description: Freeform escape hatch for consumer-specific data this schema doesn't model. Deliberately non-interoperable -- a private extension zone, not part of the typed interop surface. Recommend reverse-DNS-style keys (e.g. "com.example.internalId") when multiple parties write to it.

platform.description: Open-vocabulary platform identifier, lowercase by convention. Not a closed enum -- platform names and brands rename (Twitter -> X) or launch faster than a schema revision cycle would keep up with; a closed enum would require a schema change for every rename or new platform. Consumers needing a fixed display list or icon should map this open string at their own presentation layer.

platformId.description: Platform-assigned stable identifier, when known. Handles are mutable and sometimes transferable (an X handle can change hands or be renamed) while the id a platform assigns internally usually is not -- store platformId when available and treat handle as the display form, not the identity.

preference.description: Rank among a person's social handles; 1 = most preferred (vCard PREF). Absent means unspecified -- do NOT treat missing as 100 (lowest). Consumers comparing preferences should ignore entries without a value.

url.description: Direct profile URL, e.g. "https://x.com/jdoe". STORED, never computed from platform + handle -- platform-to-domain mappings move (twitter.com -> x.com), so computing the URL on read would silently break for every renamed platform.

title: Social/messaging handle
